svg.title: Annex A2 · Peru collector: the local server
svg.desc: The Peru collector: kit and installation, scheduled task with retries, download with robots.txt and classifier, ENFEN PDFs, extra measurements, push to data-peru, heartbeat and site refresh.
svg.text: Annex A2 · Peru collector: the local server

A Python program on a computer inside Peru (Windows, macOS or Linux) fetches every night what does not answer outside the country and pushes it to the data-peru branch. A person installs it with the kit; if the machine was off,
collection catches up on its own.
Details these boxes of the full diagram: Peru collector, data-peru branch, Collector kit and check, Peru machine operator.
Kit .zip · INSTALL and VERIFY · Windows, macOS,
fixed list, peru-server URLs and ENFEN PDFs; live

g.title: 1. Collector kit → Machine operator: kit .zip and VERIFY. The person downloads recolector-peru.zip from the recolector-kit release. The machine does not update itself.
2. Machine operator → Scheduled task: INSTALL with the token. The installer stores the token in .env, installs Python and git if missing and registers the 21:00 task.
3. Machine operator → VERIFY: runs VERIFY. Checks the machine and leaves the report for the maintainers; with --probar-tarea it fires the real task.
4. Scheduled task → Run start: 21:00 and retries. Each trigger runs the service; if today's copy is already there, it does nothing. That way it recovers a night with the machine off.
5. Run start → Token and registry: token from .env. Without a token nothing can be pushed: the run ends with a clear message and a hint to fix it.
6. Token and registry → Download: fixed list and peru-server. Its fixed-list URLs plus those the registry assigns to Peru, and their rules for following PDFs.
7. Live robots.txt → Download: robots.txt rules. A forbidden path is not requested; if robots.txt does not answer, that server is skipped tonight.
8. ENFEN portal → Download: API, listing and PDFs. The official communiqué arrives even though the portal does not answer the cloud.
9. ICEN over https (IGP) → Download: ICEN https. Kept like the rest; Actions also has the http version.
10. SENAMHI, ANA, IMARPE… → Download: archive pages. The original is kept as a backup for when a reader exists.
11. Download → ENFEN PDFs and links: listings → PDFs. The PDFs are looked up in the listings that answered tonight.
12. ENFEN PDFs and links → Extra measurements: unmeasured URLs. With the time left it measures the registry URLs nobody measured from Peru.
13. Extra measurements → Tonight's copy: measurements in index.json. The measurements go in index.json and the weekly probe adds them to the registry.
14. data-peru branch → Tonight's copy: copies up to 72 h old. Before pushing it reads the previous copy and keeps each URL that failed tonight, marked carried.
15. Tonight's copy → data-peru branch: commit and push. git without credential helpers or prompts: nobody would answer them in a scheduled task.
16. Tonight's copy → Heartbeat only: nothing answered. An empty copy would replace the last good one: only the heartbeat is pushed.
17. data-peru branch → Asks for a site refresh: after pushing. If a run is in progress, the new one queues. If the request fails, the 23:37 run uses the copy anyway.
18. Run start → Desktop alert: failures or expiring token. Each run's state decides whether to alert the person.

Collector kit. recolector-kit.yml builds the .zip with the code, the installers and a registry copy, test-installs it on Windows, macOS and Linux and publishes it in the recolector-kit release. when kit, python/enso/ or registry changes merge. Technology: GitHub Actions, GitHub Releases.

g.title: Machine operator. Downloads the kit, runs INSTALL and pastes a fine-grained GitHub token (this repository only, Contents read and write). A new kit is installed with UPDATE.

g.title: Scheduled task. 21:00 Lima and then every 30 min until 23:30, plus at login or power-on. Each trigger runs collector_service --programado. Technology: Programador de tareas, launchd, cron, systemd, Docker.
g.text: 21:00 Lima and then every 30 min until
23:30, plus at login or power-on. Each trigger

g.title: VERIFY. Checks Python, git, the token and its expiry, access to the sources, the scheduled task and the age of the latest copy; leaves a report in logs/ to send. Technology: collector_check.py.

g.title: Desktop alert. After 2 failures in a row, or if the token expires in under 21 days, it shows a desktop alert (once a day). Each run's result is kept in estado.json.

g.title: Run start. Takes the token from .env, writes a rotating log that never shows the token, takes the lock (never runs twice) and only goes on if today's 21:00 copy is missing. a hung run is cut at 45 min. Technology: collector_service.py.

log that never shows the token, takes the lock
(never runs twice) and only goes on if today's
a hung run is cut at 45 min

g.title: Token and registry. Checks the token with the GitHub API and records when it expires. Reads registry/sources.json from main with the token; if it cannot, it uses the kit's copy. Technology: GitHub API.
g.text: Checks the token with the GitHub API and
token; if it cannot, it uses the kit's copy.

a.title: Annex A1: Sources, reachability and registry

g.title: Download. Requests its fixed list and the registry's peru-server URLs, each with its alternatives. Classifies every answer like Actions and n8n: it never keeps anti-bot checks or unexpected formats. 40 s per request, 25 min in total. Technology: peru_collector.py, httpx, reach.py.

peru-server URLs, each with its alternatives.

g.title: ENFEN PDFs and links. From the ENFEN listing it derives the communiqué PDFs and the two latest technical reports (up to 20 MB) and follows the links the registry asks for.

g.title: Extra measurements. Measures, without keeping them, up to 60 registry URLs with no measurement from Peru (unmeasured, suspected geoblock or down): that is how the registry can confirm a geoblock.

g.title: data-peru branch. Each push replaces the contents; git history keeps the previous ones. The pipeline uses copies up to 7 days old and warns at 36 h. Technology: git push, enso-relay/1.

a.title: Annex A4: Download in GitHub Actions and per-source fallbacks

g.title: Heartbeat only. If no source answered, it pushes only heartbeat.json (“sin-fuentes”) and leaves the last good copy intact: that tells a machine that is off apart from sources that are down.
g.text: If no source answered, it pushes only
the last good copy intact: that tells a machine
that is off apart from sources that are down.

g.title: Asks for a site refresh. After pushing a copy it sends repository_dispatch enso-refresh: the daily update runs right away instead of waiting for 23:37. Technology: GitHub API.
